screens_reviewed: Two scroll captures of audit/[placeId]/[step] at step 3 (Access domain): the StepHeader + step pill rail + section-intro card + first question rows (08), and a deeper scroll through more presence/condition question rows (09). Persistent bottom FooterNav (Back / Save & exit / Next) visible in both.
verdict: Functionally the step wizard is well structured and the content column is correctly constrained on iPad via getResponsiveContentContainerStyle, so it is not a naively stretched phone layout. However the screen was requested in dark theme yet renders the light/cream palette: it imports the static module-level designSystem instead of the theme-aware useDesignSystem() hook, so it ignores the auditor's dark-mode, font-scale, and dyslexic-font preferences entirely. It also under-uses the large iPad canvas by stacking short answer options full-width down a ~1000px column instead of laying them out in a grid.

critical_issues.issue: The screen was captured in dark theme but renders the light/cream palette (cream background, white cards, dark-green selected rows). The route imports the static light-only token set `designSystem` (import at [step].tsx:23) and both getSurveyPalette ([step].tsx:1787) and getStepTone ([step].tsx:1774) build their palettes from designSystem.colors, which is hard-wired to lightColors via `export const designSystem = { colors: lightColors, ... }` (lib/design-system.ts:453-460). It never calls useDesignSystem(), so an auditor in dark mode still gets the full light UI on this multi-screen survey flow.
critical_issues.evidence: Both images show the light palette (#FBFAF6 background, #1E... not used); [step].tsx:23 imports static `designSystem`; lib/design-system.ts:453-460 binds designSystem.colors to lightColors; useDesignSystem (lib/design-system.ts:501) is the theme-aware path the rest of the app uses (e.g. components/ui/Card.tsx:1753).
critical_issues.fix: Switch the screen to the theme-aware hook: call `const designSystem = useDesignSystem()` at the top of AuditStepScreen and thread it (or its colors) into getSurveyPalette/getStepTone instead of importing the static `designSystem`. The shared ui/* primitives already do this; this route is the outlier.

critical_issues.issue: Every label uses raw `Text`/`Paragraph` from tamagui (import [step].tsx:22) with hard-coded numeric fontSize (e.g. QuestionCard fontSize={16} [step].tsx:1169, StepHeader title fontSize={30} [step].tsx:613) rather than ScaledText/ScaledParagraph. Because the screen also never reads useDesignSystem/fontScale, the auditor's text-size and dyslexia-friendly font preferences have no effect on this long survey — exactly where legibility matters most for field use.
critical_issues.evidence: [step].tsx:22 imports Text/Paragraph from tamagui; ScaledText (components/ui/ScaledText.tsx:2295) is the scaling drop-in used elsewhere; pack header line `design_system_components_used: (none)` confirms no shared primitives are used.
critical_issues.fix: Replace tamagui Text/Paragraph with components/ui/ScaledText (ScaledText / ScaledParagraph) so explicit fontSize/lineHeight multiply by fontScale, and source fonts from useDesignSystem() to pick up the dyslexic set.

critical_issues.issue: On the ~1040px iPad content track, short answer options ('Yes?', 'No?', 'Poor?', 'Acceptable?', 'Great?') each render as a full-width row stacked vertically. OptionGrid is a plain vertical YStack with no column logic ([step].tsx:1255-1270), so a two-word answer produces a tap target ~1000px wide with the label hugging the far left, wasting most of the canvas and forcing excess vertical scrolling through the long survey. The component is literally named OptionGrid but renders a single column.
critical_issues.evidence: Image 08/09 show every option spanning the full card width with left-aligned short labels; OptionGrid renders `<YStack gap="$2">{options.map(... SelectionButton)}</YStack>` with no columns ([step].tsx:1255-1270).
critical_issues.fix: When layout.isTablet, lay options out in 2-3 columns (XStack flexWrap with flexBasis, or a responsive grid) so short choices form a compact grid; keep the single-column fallback on phones where SelectionButton's wrap behavior is needed.

improvements.suggestion: These hand-rolled surfaces duplicate the shared components/ui/Card treatment (rounded, borderWidth, boxShadow). Adopting the shared Card (which is theme-aware via useDesignSystem) would both fix the dark-theme issue and reduce drift from the design system.
improvements.evidence: components/ui/Card.tsx:1752 provides raised/flat/muted variants; pack reports design_system_components_used: (none).

improvements.suggestion: On iPad the step rail (StepHeader pills) and the active section could become a master-detail / two-pane layout (persistent step navigator on the left, current section on the right) using the available width, rather than stacking the pill rail above a narrow-feeling single column. responsive-layout-tokens already exposes twoPaneGap/supportRailWidth for tablets.
improvements.evidence: lib/responsive-layout-tokens.ts:818-845 defines supportRailWidth/twoPaneGap for tablets; screen currently stacks everything vertically ([step].tsx:439-477).

improvements.suggestion: If full-width rows are kept, the green selected indicator reads as a large solid bar with tiny left-aligned text on iPad. Consider a leading radio/check affordance so selection state is legible at width, rather than relying on the whole bar filling green.
improvements.evidence: Images 08/09 show selected rows as wide solid-green bars with small left text; SelectionButton sets textAlign left, flexShrink 1 ([step].tsx:1308-1313).

tamagui_notes: Screen imports the static module-level `designSystem` (lib/design-system.ts:453) instead of useDesignSystem(); this is why dark theme and accessibility preferences are not applied (see ignores-dark-theme-static-design-system).
Raw tamagui Text/Paragraph used throughout ([step].tsx:22) bypass ScaledText/ScaledParagraph, so numeric font sizes do not respect fontScale.

getResponsiveContentContainerStyle + useResponsiveLayout are correctly wired ([step].tsx:434, 85), so the content column is properly centered/maxWidth-constrained on iPad — the layout is not a blindly stretched phone screen.
Footer uses paddingBottom: bottomInset + 12 ([step].tsx:1680) so it respects the bottom safe-area inset.
platform_notes: iPad content width IS constrained via the responsive content container (contentMaxWidth ~1040 on narrow tablet per responsive-layout-tokens.ts:779), so the screen avoids edge-to-edge text. The main iPad gap is intra-card: answer options stay single-column full-width instead of a grid, and there is no split-view/master-detail use of the spare width.
Step pills set minWidth 108 and flexWrap ([step].tsx:686, 669) which wrap acceptably on the wide canvas; no tap-target concern (rows are well above 44pt given py=$3).
No modal/sheet is presented on this route, so iPad sheet-sizing is not applicable here.
not_assessable: Exact WCAG contrast ratios of the rendered light palette (the requested dark palette is not actually shown, so the intended dark-mode contrast cannot be judged from these images).
Runtime states not shown: loading/blocked/error notice cards, the unanswered-questions confirm Alert, and saving spinner in the Next button.
Split-view / Stage Manager multitasking behavior (single full-window capture only).
score_rationale: Usable with clear problems: the underlying wizard structure, content-width constraint, and safe-area handling are solid (7-8 territory), but the screen ships the light palette in dark mode and ignores font-scale/dyslexic-font preferences because it bypasses useDesignSystem() — a real, verifiable defect across a long survey flow — and under-uses the iPad canvas with full-width single-column options. The theme defect plus weak large-canvas adaptation pull it to a 5.
